question: What is the primary purpose of performing a vulvar swab?

options.A: To collect samples for identifying infectious organisms
options.B: To perform a routine bimanual pelvic examination
options.C: To administer localized topical pain medication
options.D: To measure the pH level of the vaginal canal

explanation: Vulvar swabbing targets microbiological analysis to diagnose specific infections affecting the external genitalia. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why is targeted antimicrobial therapy important following a vulvar swab?

options.A: It guarantees complete immunity against future infections
options.B: It immediately reverses chronic tissue inflammation
options.C: It prevents the overuse of broad-spectrum medications
options.D: It eliminates the need for patient hygiene education

explanation: Identifying the exact pathogen allows clinicians to prescribe specific drugs rather than relying on broad-spectrum agents that promote resistance. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which structure lies directly medial to the labia majora?
explanation: The labia minora are the delicate inner folds positioned directly inside the larger outer labial folds. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h2)

question: The vestibule contains which of the following anatomical features?
explanation: The vestibule is the enclosed space containing the openings for both the urethra and the vagina. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h2)

question: What is an essential component of every vulvar swab collection kit?
explanation: A transport medium keeps the collected microbial sample viable until it reaches the laboratory for analysis. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h3)

question: Why must a nurse gather all required equipment before positioning the patient?

options.A: To ensure the laboratory processes the specimen immediately
options.B: To comply with federal hospital financial auditing standards
options.C: To minimize patient anxiety and avoid interrupting the procedure
options.D: To reduce the total amount of medical waste generated

explanation: Having supplies ready prevents awkward interruptions while the patient is in a vulnerable lithotomy position. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the primary reason for properly draping a patient during a vulvar swab?

options.A: To prevent the collection swab from drying out in the air
options.B: To maintain patient modesty and dignity throughout the procedure
options.C: To create a sterile operating field for surgical incisions
options.D: To keep the examination room at a comfortable temperature

explanation: Appropriate draping protects patient privacy and reduces the psychological discomfort of an intimate examination. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h4)

question: Which body position is standard for performing a vulvar examination?
explanation: The dorsal lithotomy position provides optimal visual and physical access to the external genitalia. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h4)

question: How should the nurse handle the swab after collecting the specimen from a lesion?

options.A: Immediately insert it into the transport tube
options.B: Rinse the swab tip under running tap water
options.C: Place it on a sterile gauze pad to air dry
options.D: Store it in an open kidney basin at room temperature

explanation: Prompt placement into the transport medium preserves the integrity and viability of the collected specimen. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why is it important to avoid touching surrounding healthy skin when swabbing a lesion?

options.A: It prevents diluting the sample with normal skin flora
options.B: It keeps the transport medium from changing color
options.C: It ensures the swab remains completely dry
options.D: It stops the patient from feeling any sharp pain

explanation: Targeting only the affected site ensures the laboratory analyzes the pathogen causing the issue rather than normal skin bacteria. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h5)

question: When must the specimen container be labeled with patient details?

options.A: After returning from the clinical laboratory
options.B: Before entering the patient examination room
options.C: At the end of the nursing shift
options.D: At the bedside immediately after collection

explanation: Labeling specimens at the bedside prevents mix-ups and ensures positive patient identification. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is a major consequence of delaying specimen transport to the laboratory?

options.A: Degradation of pathogens leading to inaccurate results
options.B: Immediate crystallization of the transport medium
options.C: Automatic rejection of the sample by the billing department
options.D: Permanent discoloration of the collection swab shaft

explanation: Prompt transport prevents organism death or overgrowth, which distorts diagnostic test accuracy. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h6)

question: Where should contaminated disposable swabbing materials be discarded?
explanation: Contaminated items carrying bodily fluids must go into biohazard bins to prevent environmental spread of infection. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h7)

question: Which practice is most effective in preventing cross-contamination between patients?

options.A: Keeping the examination room door tightly locked
options.B: Using the same examination table without cleaning it
options.C: Performing hand hygiene and changing gloves between cases
options.D: Wearing sterile gloves for all non-invasive patient talks

explanation: Hand hygiene and fresh gloves stop the transmission of microorganisms from one patient to another. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h7)

question: Which detail must be included in the nursing documentation after a vulvar swab?

options.A: Name of the manufacturing company of the swabs
options.B: Detailed financial cost of the laboratory test
options.C: Date, time, and anatomical site of the swab
options.D: Exact room temperature during the procedure

explanation: Documentation must capture procedural specifics like timing and location for clinical tracking and safety. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h8)

question: A patient asks when she will get her test results. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: Explain the follow-up process and when results are expected
options.B: Tell her that results are usually available within five minutes
options.C: Promise her that the test will definitely come back negative
options.D: Instruct her to call the laboratory director directly tonight

explanation: Providing clear follow-up instructions reduces patient anxiety and ensures timely receipt of treatment if needed. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T15#GNS221_U2_T15_h8)
